newsitem.title: GERMANY: Preussag may accept lower stake in Bewag.
newsitem.headline: Preussag may accept lower stake in Bewag.

text.p: German utility PreussenElektra may accept a lower stake in Berlin's Bewag, to allow the bid by a consortium led by Southern Corp of the U.S. to go ahead, the Berliner Zeitung reported.
German cartel authorities had reservations about Berlin's sale of its remaining 50.8 percent stake in Bewag because of PreussenElektra's role in the Southern-led group.
PreussenElektra and its parent Veba AG have other interests in the Berlin region that, added to the Bewag stake, could give them a market-dominating position, cartel authorities feared.
The sale would bring 3.19 billion marks to the cash-strapped Berlin government.
Under the original plan Southern, the largest utility in the U.S., was to acquire a 23.6 percent stake and management control of Bewag.
PreussenElektra and Viag, which already hold 10 percent, were to buy an additional 13.6 percent.
PreussenElektra signalled to the cartel office that it would be prepared to accept a 23 percent stake in Bewag, the Berliner Zeitung reported.
It also quoted sources near Viag as saying the deal would not collapse because of the cartel office's reservations about Veba's role.
PreussenElektra and Viag officials declined to comment on the report.
